sources.snippet: Even into the 21st century, queens continue to shape society. Queen Elizabeth II, the longest-reigning monarch in British history, served as a symbol of continuity and resilience from 1952 until her death in 2022. Her reign spanned post-war recovery, the decline of the British Empire, and the modern digital age. Despite having limited political power, her presence provided stability during times of crisis, including wars, recessions, and the global COVID-19 pandemic. Outside of the West, [...] In classical antiquity, Cleopatra VII, the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, stands out as a figure of intelligence, charisma, and political skill. Fluent in multiple languages and deeply educated, Cleopatra formed alliances with powerful Roman leaders such as Julius Caesar and Mark Antony. Her life and reign have inspired countless stories, dramatizations, and scholarly debates, often focusing on her ability to use both diplomacy and charm in a male-dominated world. [...] In the modern era, the most iconic queen is arguably Queen Elizabeth I of England. Her reign, known as the Elizabethan era, is celebrated for its flourishing of English drama, led by playwrights like William Shakespeare, and the expansion of English influence overseas. Elizabeth skillfully navigated religious and political divisions in her country and famously never married, referring to herself as the "Virgin Queen" and dedicating herself wholly to her realm.
